role.altitude: The week is still with people: the supervisor consult, the equipment demonstration, the rule explanation, and the food conversation. Less of it is hunting a program line, a care card, a house rule, or a unit price.
reach: The supervisor decides the program in the consult.
The tenant sees the equipment used.
A client hears one food choice they can afford.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a program note the supervisor did not say
Stop a demonstration when the equipment is unsafe
Decline a food suggestion the client cannot afford or should not eat
role.ambitious_version: Before the visit the program line, the care card, the house rule and the price card are open. They still consult, still demonstrate, still explain, and still recommend.

steps.what: Read the open program line concerning these individual families.
Consult the supervisor concerning programs for these individual families.
Write the program note agreed for each family.

tasks.design: The consult with the supervisor stays the full meeting. The program line in {OTHER} is the record the social worker already registered, so this read finds that line rather than retyping a referral, and the note afterwards adds only the status the supervisor just said. Nothing records the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program sat in a referral mail, and the note after the consult repeated the family and the program.
tasks.enabler_now: The case file can open the program line the social worker already registered, so the note adds only the status.
tasks.still_hard: Which program a family should keep is the supervisor's call, made in the room with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears what the supervisor actually decided and can tell a firm decision from a maybe.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the program line and retyping the family and the program.

reach.task: Decide the program in the consult
reach.learn: The note stores the status they spoke, on the line the social worker already registered.
The note does not replace the written report to the client.

evidence.claim: Summaries of municipal kitchen-table talks saved little time because the consultants kept their own notes, and the summaries were weaker on mental complaints and on several problems at once.

A review of transcription tools in social work found notes that invented suicidal ideation and a food item the visit did not contain, and one council's own check was less positive than the vendor's evaluation.
Eligibility for public assistance and services, including healthcare, by or for public authorities is high-risk, and a decision on eligibility may not rest solely on automated processing.
An investigation under the Dutch Social Support Act is followed within six weeks by a written report to the client.
Health data is a special category.
In the Netherlands, recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one consult, one set of families, in a mid-size welfare or housing organisation. The assistant does not decide eligibility and does not write the client's report. The prior meetings share of 72.1 is this consult, recorded as a meeting, share 74.

Program-line contract, produced by the social worker who registered the assignment, outside this task: family id, program id, status, start date. The line opens with the family, which is why the read drops to 80 percent; they still read it. If the line is empty, the supervisor states it in the meeting and the read is not shorter.

Note contract: family id and program id come from that line. The supervisor is the producer of the status, spoken in the consult. The assistant writes it in the note step, which is why that step stays at 70 percent. They still write one line of what was agreed. If the line is empty they type the family and the program as well.

The consult is not the six-week written report to the client. Nothing scores eligibility, and nothing records the meeting, so the Dutch works-council consent for recording is not this build. Other countries' staff-recording rules differ. Family support can be special-category data. The case system running is not the assistant's time.

The prior that a model is needed, 0.29, and the clear-gain prior of 0.08, are the meeting. A generated summary is refused because kitchen-table summaries saved little time and generated notes have invented facts. Upkeep of 0.4 hours per 100 is correcting a note filed on the wrong family.
unknowns: Whether this organisation's case file stores family id, program id, status and start date.
Whether family program notes are treated as health data here.
research_questions: How often is the program line missing, so the read is not shorter?
How often is a program note filed on the wrong family?

already_counted.description: Reading the program line once it is open.
The consult with the supervisor, unchanged.
Writing the status the supervisor said.

incremental.description: Correct a program note filed on the wrong family. The status they heard stays in the note step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A consult where the program line is missing and they reconstruct it with the supervisor lands near 0. A consult where the line is already on the file and they add only the status lands near 4. The meeting stays full length.

steps.what: Read the care card for this tenant equipment.
Demonstrate use and care of the equipment for this tenant.
Tick that this tenant was shown the equipment.

tasks.design: The demonstration in the home stays the full visit. The care card in {DOCS} opens on the equipment id the housing maintenance lead stored, so they read those steps instead of hunting a binder, and the tick stores that this tenant was shown it without copying the model number. They still show every step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The care steps sat in a binder, and the visit note repeated the model number.
tasks.enabler_now: The care card can open with the equipment, so the tick confirms the tenant without copying the model number.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this tenant can work the equipment safely is seen only while they try it.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant can stop the demonstration when a guard is missing or the tenant is at risk.
tasks.altitude: The visit stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the care card and copying the model number.

reach.task: Use the equipment after the demonstration
reach.learn: The card they were shown is the care card maintenance stored.
The tick says the tenant was shown the card, not that the equipment is safe.

evidence.claim: Showing a tenant how to use and care for equipment stays with the person in the home. A stored care card can open the steps; it does not perform them.
A note that names the tenant is personal data and is kept to the equipment shown and the date.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one tenant, one piece of equipment, in the home. This is not a repair and not a training course. The prior in-person share of 87.1 is the demonstration, share 88.

Care-card contract, produced by the housing maintenance lead, outside this task: equipment id, use steps, care steps. The card opens with the equipment, which is why the read drops to 85 percent; they still read the steps before showing them. If the card is empty, the card fixed to the machine is the fallback and the read is not shorter.

Tick contract: equipment id comes from the care card. Tenant id and name come from the tenancy list, produced by housing allocation, outside this task. The assistant is the producer of the shown flag, set in this step after the demonstration, which is why the tick stays at 90 percent. If the tenancy list is empty they write the name.

The clear-gain prior of 0.02 matches a small net. No model watches the demonstration. The store opening the card is not the assistant's time. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 is correcting a tick on the wrong tenant.
unknowns: Whether this organisation stores a care card with equipment id, use steps and care steps.
Whether the tenancy list is on the same record as the care card.
research_questions: How often is the care card missing, so the read is the card on the machine?
How often is the shown tick on the wrong tenant?

already_counted.description: Reading the care card once it is open.
Ticking that the tenant was shown the equipment.

incremental.description: Correct a tick on the wrong tenant. The demonstration itself is unchanged.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A visit where the care card is on the machine and they write the model number lands near 0. A visit where the card opens and the tick only confirms the tenant lands near 1. The demonstration stays full length.

steps.what: Read the rules established by the owner or management.
Explain the sanitation rules, the maintenance requirements and the parking regulations.
Note which rule was explained to this tenant.
Send the housing office the note of which rule was explained.

tasks.design: Explaining the rule to the tenant stays the full conversation. The rule list in {DOCS} opens on the topic the owner or management already wrote, so they read that line instead of searching the booklet, and the note stores the rule id rather than recopying the text. The note to the housing office in {EMAIL} stays the same length and does not grant an exception.
tasks.previous_blocker: The house rules were a booklet, and the note recopied the rule text.
tasks.enabler_now: The rule list can open on the topic, so the note stores the rule id the owner or management already wrote.
tasks.still_hard: Which part of the rule matters for this tenant, and how to say it so they can follow it, is the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant can tell a question about the rule from a request to break it.
tasks.altitude: The conversation stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the rule and recopying it.

reach.learn: The line they hear is the rule the owner or management already wrote.
The note names the rule id and the tenant. It does not change the rule.

evidence.claim: House rules on sanitation, maintenance and parking are quoted from the list the owner or management keeps. The explanation to the tenant stays with the person.
A note that names the tenant and the rule explained is personal data and does not by itself decide a benefit.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one tenant, one question, about house rules the owner or management already set. This is not an eligibility decision and not a sanction. The prior in-person share of 68.6 is the explanation, share 70. The office note matches the mail share of 6.3.

Rule-list contract, produced by the owner or management, outside this task: rule id, topic, short line. Topics include sanitation, maintenance and parking. The topic opens the line, which is why the read drops to 75 percent; they still read it before explaining. If the list is empty, the printed booklet is the fallback and the read is not shorter.

Note contract: rule id comes from that list. Tenant id and name come from the tenancy list, produced by housing allocation, outside this task. The assistant is the producer of the explained flag, set in the note step, which is why it stays at 80 percent. If the tenancy list is empty they write the name. They do not recopy the rule text when the id is filled.

The office mail is unchanged because the design does not shorten that writing. It sends the note. It does not promise an exception. The prior that automation could do nearly all of this, 0.37, is not a licence to shorten the explanation; the clear-gain prior is 0.09. No model drafts what to say. Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is correcting a note on the wrong tenant.
unknowns: Whether this organisation stores house rules with a rule id, a topic and a short line.
Whether the housing office already receives this note by mail.
research_questions: How often are the house rules only a booklet, so the read is not shorter?
How often is the rule note on the wrong tenant?

already_counted.description: Reading the rule once the topic opens it.

incremental.description: Correct a rule note filed on the wrong tenant. The explanation stays in the conversation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A talk where the house rules are a booklet and the note recopies the rule lands near 0. A talk where the topic opens the rule and the note stores the rule id lands near 3.5. The explanation stays full length.

steps.what: Read the unit price and the nutrition line for those selections.
Recommend alternate economical and nutritional food choices.
Write the food choice the client took.

tasks.design: Watching what the client picks and recommending a choice stay the full conversation. The price card in {DOCS} already holds the unit price and a short nutrition line the programme buyer copied from the packet, so they read that card instead of adding a receipt, and the note in {OTHER} stores the item the client took. Nothing suggests a food the client did not discuss.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unit prices were added off the packet, and the note afterwards described the food in prose.
tasks.enabler_now: The price card can hold the unit price and a short nutrition line, so the note stores the item the client took.
tasks.still_hard: What this client can afford, and what they should eat, is judged in the shop with them.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant can see a choice that is cheap and still wrong for this client.
tasks.altitude: The shop conversation stays the same length. The shorter piece is adding a unit price and describing the item in prose.

reach.task: Choose a food they can afford
reach.learn: The choice they hear is the assistant's, after seeing what they picked.
The card holds item, unit price and a short nutrition line copied from the packet.

evidence.claim: A review of transcription tools in social work found notes that invented suicidal ideation and a food item the visit did not contain, and one council's own check was less positive than the vendor's evaluation.
A food budget can be a calculator of stored prices. The recommendation of what this client should eat stays with the person.
Health data is a special category.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one client, one shop or kitchen visit. The assistant does not prescribe a diet and does not decide a benefit. The prior in-person share of 85.4 is observing and recommending, shares 52 and 34.

Price-card contract, produced by the programme buyer, outside this task, copied from the packet label: item id, unit price, a short nutrition line. No model reads the packet. The card opens for the item they saw, which is why the read drops to 80 percent; they still read it. If the card has no line, they read the packet and the read is not shorter.

Note contract: item id comes from the price card. Client id comes from the client list, produced by the programme enrolment, outside this task. The client is the producer of the choice, spoken in the recommendation. The assistant writes the item id in the note step, which is why it stays at 75 percent. If the card or the list is empty they type the item and the name. The note does not add a food the client did not discuss.

The prior that a model is needed, 0.53, and the clear-gain prior of 0.26, are not a licence to shorten the recommendation. Generated notes have invented a food the visit did not contain. Diet notes can be special-category data. Whether a data-protection assessment is required is for the customer to confirm. Upkeep of 0.4 hours per 100 is correcting a note that names the wrong item.
unknowns: Whether this programme stores a price card with item id, unit price and a short nutrition line.
Whether a food note is treated as health data here.
research_questions: How often is the price card missing, so the price is read off the packet?
How often does the food note name an item the client did not take?

already_counted.description: Reading the unit price once the card is open.
Writing the item the client took.

incremental.description: Correct a food note that names the wrong item. The recommendation they spoke stays in the conversation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A shop where prices are read off the packets lands near 0. A shop where the price card has the unit price and the note stores the item id lands near 2. They still observe and still recommend.
